title: Spacetime causality in the study of the Hankel transform
version: arXiv:math/0509619v4, 5 March 2006; pages 1-4, 6-16, 19-20, 23-24 read through a page extraction
locator: Theorem 1 (p. 2) and its proof (pp. 2-3, 7-9); remark on one-way packets (p. 11); Theorems 2-4 (pp. 3-6)
assumptions: Klein-Gordon equation in 1+1 dimensions with m = 1; finite-energy solutions.
conclusion: Author's Theorem 1: for a finite-energy solution the energy in |x| > t tends to 0 as t tends to infinity. Author's remarks: this fails for zero mass; it follows from Hormander's pointwise estimates; he could not locate a reference and does not think it novel.
proof_status: Self-contained proof via a wave-packet representation and Hardy-space orthogonality, read. Not re-derived independently.
relevance: Supplies Lemma 1 of the massive-Minkowski note in 1+1 dimensions.
open_questions: A citable statement of the same decay in n+1 dimensions.
limits: Pages 5, 17-18, 21-22 not read. Extraction garbles some formulas.

title: Electromagnetism and time-asymmetry
assumptions: Classical Maxwell theory; an observer with access only to data in or on the past light cone.
conclusion: Author's claim: prediction requires the Sommerfeld condition of no incoming radiation, so the theory that is actually confirmed is time-asymmetric.
dependencies: Earman 1986; Wheeler and Feynman 1945, 1949: not read.
relevance: Nearest philosophical predecessor. Concerns the massless case only.
open_questions: Whether later work extends the argument to massive fields.
